title: pvProtractor
body:
## pvProtractor

ParaView's protractor: a polyline (vtkPolyLineSource) through three points, [point 1, vertex, point 2], whose angle at the vertex ParaView's interactive widget displays. In Schemaxis the output is only the polyline geometry; the angle is not written into the data, so compute it from the three points when you need the value. Use it to show an angle annotation in a scene; pvRuler is the equivalent for distances.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- ParaView's default Points has only two points, so no angle is defined; give nine numbers.
- No angle array or measurement is produced by the source itself.
- Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

Native constructor: `Protractor`. Identity: `sources/Protractor`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Points` | Flat list of nine coordinates [x1, y1, z1, xv, yv, zv, x2, y2, z2]: the first arm end point, the vertex where the angle is measured, then the second arm end point. ParaView's angle widget reads the points in exactly this order. Complete tuples of 3 values. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1]` |

